idea-plugin.name: Mkdocs
idea-plugin.description:
Support for MkDocs projects in all IntelliJ-platform IDEs.

The plugin recognizes every MkDocs site inside your project, makes it visible in the IDE and lets you create new sites without leaving the editor.

Features
  • Automatic site detection – every mkdocs.yml / mkdocs.yaml turns its directory into an MkDocs site, re-detected after every file system change.
  • Module integration – a detected site is represented by an MkDocs facet on the surrounding module; if the site belongs to no module, an own module is created. Its name is taken from site_name, falling back to the directory name. Its page in Project Structure lets the site be renamed through site_name and the technical directories along with it: the directory is moved and every reference to it – in mkdocs.yml and in the pages – follows, while docs_dir and site_dir are written back into the configuration file.
  • Project view – the site root is labelled with the site name and badged, and the documentation directory (docs_dir) as well as the assets and stylesheets directories are marked.
  • File icons – own icons for mkdocs.yml / mkdocs.yaml, for the Markdown pages below docs_dir, for a requirements.txt sitting directly next to the configuration file and for every style sheet listed in extra_css.
  • Site Page tool window – one tab per detected site, each showing the navigation written under nav. A node is labelled with the title from nav, else with the first # heading of the page, else with the file name, followed in grey by the file name and, for a page in a subdirectory, its relative path. Sections carry an own MkDocs folder icon. Double clicking opens the page in the editor or the address in the browser; entries pointing nowhere are kept and marked.
  • Path references – the entries of extra_css, the targets of nav, theme.logo, theme.favicon, docs_dir and site_dir point at the file or directory they name: Ctrl+click follows the path, completion offers what is there, renaming rewrites the entry, and a path leading nowhere is reported — except site_dir, which names the build output.
  • Gutter icons – every one of those paths carries an icon opening the target with one click, a file with the icon it carries elsewhere in the IDE, docs_dir and site_dir with the badge of their directory.
  • Path check – forbidden or control characters, empty segments, a segment ending in a dot or a space, an absolute path, a drive letter and a .. leaving the site are reported as errors; what only breaks on other operating systems — backslash separator, reserved Windows names, non-ASCII characters, spaces in segments — as warnings. site_dir names the build output and may lie outside the site, so an absolute path, a drive letter and a .. are not reported there.
  • Site creation – New → MkDocs Site walks through layout (docs_dir, assets, stylesheets, site_dir), site metadata (site_name, site_author, site_description, site_url), repository (repo_name, repo_url), copyright and optional features, and writes the configuration, the documentation directory and a start page.
  • Repository detection – repository address, repository name and author are prefilled from Git, and an entry deviating from the local repository is reported.
  • Copyright integration – the notice is taken from the IDE's Copyright profiles, with a choice when several are configured and no default is set.
  • Metadata banner – a missing site_name, site_author or site_description is reported by a banner above mkdocs.yml / mkdocs.yaml, each with a fix adding the key.
  • JSON schema – mkdocs.yaml is mapped to the MkDocs schema, which the bundled catalogue only offers for mkdocs.yml.
  • Directory completion – missing site directories are suggested in the New Directory dialog.
  • Feature extension point – siteFeature allows optional MkDocs extensions (Angular Material, I18N, Mike) to plug into the creation wizard.
  • Angular Material – a site using the Material theme carries the Angular Material facet, detected from theme.name. The facet can be selected in the creation wizard and added or removed in the Project Structure dialog, which writes the theme into mkdocs.yml or takes it out again. It is bound to the MkDocs facet and disappears with it.
  • Material schema – a site carrying the Angular Material facet is edited against a refined schema for the blocks the theme fills: all 28 flags of theme.features with a description each, theme.palette in both its shapes with the colours and schemes of the theme, theme.font, theme.language, theme.icon, theme.direction, theme.logo, theme.favicon, theme.custom_dir, and social, analytics, consent, generator and status below extra. It stands in front of the MkDocs schema instead of replacing it and is bundled with the plugin, so it works offline.
  • Markdown extensions – an extension the configuration forces, because a feature flag does not render without it, is reported above mkdocs.yml as an error, with a fix adding it together with the options it needs. Everything the theme merely builds on is a weak warning that can be switched off. Quick documentation explains each entry of markdown_extensions.
  • Path values – theme.custom_dir and the entries of extra_javascript, in both shapes MkDocs 1.6 accepts, are file references like every other path, and an intention creates the target a path points at.
  • Material icons – the icons of the installed mkdocs-material are completed in mkdocs.yml and as the shorthands :material-check: in the pages, each showing its drawing, and every place mkdocs.yml names an icon is covered. An icon already written shows its drawing in the editor as well, in front of the name and in front of the shorthand. The installation is found through pip show mkdocs-material, or chosen under Tools → MkDocs → Material, which lists what was found and takes a directory of your own – checked against the metadata pip wrote there before it is accepted. While no installation can be found, mkdocs.yml says so in a banner leading to that page.
  • Material style sheets – the custom properties of the theme (--md-…) are completed inside CSS files.
  • Material origin – the keys a site owes to the Material theme are marked as such: an icon in front of theme.features, theme.palette, theme.font, theme.icon, theme.direction and the theme's keys below extra, and the same icon on the completion entries coming from the theme, in mkdocs.yml, in the pages and in the style sheets. What MkDocs itself reads stays unmarked.
  • Template overrides – the context menu of a site root creates the override directory, the selected templates with a working Jinja scaffold, and theme.custom_dir pointing at them, in one undoable step. Live templates for the Jinja blocks come with it.
The current implementation status is tracked in STATUS.md.

Documentation: kleinerhacker.github.io/intellij-plugin.mkdocs
